candidates.name: procyclidine (1-cyclohexyl-1-phenyl-3-(pyrrolidin-1-yl)propan-1-ol)
candidates.rationale: Phenyl 13C at 143.3/128.2/126.7/125.7 (14-17). Pyrrolidine NCH2 at 53.8 (19) and CH2 at 23.3 (29). Chain NCH2 at 52.1 (21) and CH2 at 34.8 (23). Cyclohexyl CH at 49.2 (22). Five distinct cyclohexyl CH2 carbons (24-28) appear because the ring sits next to a stereocentre. The tertiary C-OH is hidden under CDCl3 (18). Two rings plus the phenyl give DoU 6.

candidates.name: 1-cyclopentyl-1-phenyl-3-(piperidin-1-yl)propan-1-ol
candidates.rationale: Isomeric amino carbinol with the same formula: phenyl (14-17), NCH2 carbons (19-21) and a carbinol C hidden at 77.6. It is less consistent because the cyclopentyl CH would sit nearer 47 ppm and piperidine shows a 24.5 ppm CH2 pattern.

candidates.name: 1-cyclopentyl-1-phenyl-4-(pyrrolidin-1-yl)butan-1-ol
candidates.rationale: Chain-homolog isomer with the same formula: pyrrolidine (19, 29), phenyl (14-17) and a carbinol under solvent (18). It needs an extra chain CH2 and fewer ring CH2 carbons, so it fits the five ~26 ppm signals (24-28) less well.

first.reasoning_summary:
C19H29NO has DoU 6. The phenyl ring (4 DoU) shows 13C at 143.3, 128.2, 126.7 and 125.7, and 1H at 7.35 with part hidden under CDCl3. There is no carbonyl, so the remaining 2 DoU are rings. The single O is a tertiary alcohol whose carbinol carbon is hidden under the CDCl3 triplet at 77.6. N-CH2 carbons appear at 53.8, 53.7 and 52.1, with a pyrrolidine CH2 at 23.3. A CH at 49.2 and five CH2 signals at 26-27 fit a cyclohexyl ring made diastereotopic by the adjacent stereocentre, and the chain CH2 is at 34.8. Together these match procyclidine. The 1H integrals sum to about 29 H.

One gap: the 53.7 signal (id 20) has no separate assignment. It may be the second carbon of a doubled pyrrolidine NCH2 signal.

evidence.note: ArH at 7.35 and aromatic 13C at 143.3, 128.2, 126.7 and 125.7 indicate a monosubstituted phenyl.
The CH-OH methine at 3.73 sits in the alpha-oxygen range.
NCH2 1H at 2.8-3.2 and N-C 13C at 52-54 ppm fit a tertiary piperidine N.

candidates.name: 2-(4-phenylpiperidin-1-yl)cyclooctan-1-ol
candidates.rationale: Formula C19H29NO with DoU 6 (phenyl plus two rings). Phenyl carbons 14-17 and a PhCH at 2.48 (7). Piperidine NCH2 at 3.20/2.79 (4, 5) and N-C carbons 19-22. Cyclooctane CH2 carbons 23-29. The CHOH at 3.73 (3). This gives 15 distinct carbons against 15 observed.

candidates.name: 2-(4-benzylpiperidin-1-yl)cycloheptan-1-ol
candidates.rationale: Same formula and 15 distinct carbons. The benzyl CH2 at 2.48 (7), CHOH at 3.73 (3) and NCH2 at 2.79-3.20 (4, 5) fit, but the ipso carbon at 143.3 is somewhat high for a benzyl group.

candidates.name: 2-(3-phenylpiperidin-1-yl)cyclooctan-1-ol
candidates.rationale: A regioisomer with the same formula. It gives 17 distinct carbons, which is within the allowed range, but it is less symmetric than the observed spectrum suggests.

repaired.reasoning_summary: DoU 6 means a phenyl ring plus two rings and no carbonyl, so O is an alcohol and N is a tertiary amine. The earlier symmetric cyclohexyl/pyrrolidine candidate gave too few distinct carbons (13 against 15 observed), so I moved to a 4-phenylpiperidine N-linked to a cyclooctanol, which has 15 distinct carbons. The fit is imperfect: a CH-OH and CH-N carbon would normally appear near 65-72 ppm, and no 13C peak is observed there. The 53-49 ppm signals are assigned to N-C carbons and the CHOH carbon may be hidden near the solvent. Confidence is therefore moderate.
